झारखंड के सरकारी विभागों में 30-40 प्रतिशत कमीशनखोरी का आरोप, पूर्व सांसद ने दी आंदोलन की चेतावनी
पूर्व सांसद भुवनेश्वर प्रसाद मेहता ने हजारीबाग में पीडब्ल्यूडी, ग्रामीण विकास सहित कई सरकारी विभागों में भ्रष्टाचार और अनियमितताओं का ...और पढ़ें
HighLights
पूर्व सांसद मेहता ने सरकारी विभागों में भ्रष्टाचार का आरोप लगाया।
अनियमितताओं की निष्पक्ष जांच, दोषियों पर कार्रवाई की मांग की।
संवाद सहयोगी, हजारीबाग। अखिल भारतीय किसान सभा एवं झारखंड राज्य विस्थापित संघर्ष मोर्चा के अध्यक्ष सह पूर्व सांसद भुवनेश्वर प्रसाद मेहता ने राज्य के सरकारी कार्यालयों में कथित भ्रष्टाचार, कमीशनखोरी और प्रशासनिक अनियमितताओं को लेकर सरकार पर तीखा हमला बोला है।
मंगलवार को हजारीबाग परिसदन में आयोजित प्रेस वार्ता में उन्होंने पीडब्ल्यूडी, ग्रामीण विकास विभाग, जिला परिषद, विशेष प्रमंडल, भवन प्रमंडल तथा पेयजल एवं स्वच्छता विभाग समेत कई विभागों में भ्रष्टाचार का आरोप लगाया। उन्होंने मुख्यमंत्री हेमंत सोरेन से पूरे मामले की निष्पक्ष जांच कर दोषियों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग की। साथ ही चेतावनी दी कि व्यवस्था में सुधार नहीं हुआ तो पूरे झारखंड में व्यापक आंदोलन छेड़ा जाएगा।
भुवनेश्वर प्रसाद मेहता ने आरोप लगाया कि कई विकास योजनाओं में प्राक्कलित राशि से 30 से 40 प्रतिशत कम दर पर निविदा स्वीकृत होने के बावजूद कथित कमीशनखोरी का दबाव बनाया जाता है। इससे निर्माण कार्यों की गुणवत्ता प्रभावित हो रही है। उन्होंने निविदा प्रक्रिया में पारदर्शिता लाने और विकास योजनाओं की गुणवत्ता की नियमित निगरानी सुनिश्चित करने की मांग की।
प्रेस वार्ता में झारखंड स्वतंत्रता सेनानी विचार मंच के अध्यक्ष बटेश्वर प्रसाद मेहता, ऑल इंडिया यूथ फेडरेशन के प्रदेश अध्यक्ष अर्जुन कुमार, निजाम अंसारी एवं गयानाथ पांडेय उपस्थित थे।
कोनार जलापूर्ति योजना में एलएनटी की कार्यशैली पर सवाल
पूर्व सांसद ने कोनार जलापूर्ति योजना के कार्यान्वयन में लगी कंपनी एलएनटी की कार्यशैली पर भी सवाल उठाए। उन्होंने कहा कि कई स्थानों पर सड़कें खोदकर छोड़ दी गई हैं, जिससे आम लोगों को आवागमन में परेशानी हो रही है।
निर्धारित समय सीमा में काम पूरा नहीं होने के बावजूद योजना की प्राक्कलित राशि और कार्य अवधि बढ़ाए जाने पर भी उन्होंने आपत्ति जताई। उन्होंने पूरे मामले की जांच कर अनियमितता मिलने पर संबंधित कंपनी के विरुद्ध कार्रवाई की मांग की।
नगर निगम की सफाई व्यवस्था पर भी उठाए सवाल
शहर की सफाई व्यवस्था पर नाराजगी जताते हुए भुवनेश्वर प्रसाद मेहता ने कहा कि नगर निगम क्षेत्र में कई जगह कचरे का अंबार लगा है। निगम प्रशासन सफाई व्यवस्था दुरुस्त करने में गंभीरता दिखाए। वहीं, छठ महापर्व की धार्मिक आस्था से जुड़े हजारीबाग झील में फ्लोटिंग रेस्टोरेंट बनाए जाने के निर्णय पर भी उन्होंने सवाल उठाए।
उन्होंने कहा कि पर्यटन को बढ़ावा देने के लिए बड़े झील जैसे वैकल्पिक स्थान का चयन किया जा सकता था। इससे पर्यटन विकास के साथ झील की स्वच्छता और सौंदर्यीकरण को भी बढ़ावा मिलता तथा छठ घाट की धार्मिक महत्ता प्रभावित नहीं होती।

articles.full_text:
नई दिल्ली । डेस्क: इज़राइल के प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू ने मंगलवार को 26वीं केसेट के शपथ ग्रहण के दौरान दिए अपने संबोधन में चेतावनी दी कि ईरान अपने परमाणु खतरे को नए सिरे से बढ़ा रहा है. उन्होंने जोर देकर कहा कि इस अस्तित्व के खतरे को स्थायी रूप से खत्म करने का एकमात्र रास्ता अयातुल्ला शासन का पतन ही है.
नेतन्याहू ने यह भी चेताया कि इज़राइल पर जल्द ही अंतरराष्ट्रीय दबाव बनाया जाएगा कि वह ईरान को एक परमाणु शक्ति के रूप में स्वीकार करे और उसे मिटाने की मंशा रखने वाले इस भयानक शासन को सहन करे. इसके अलावा, उन्होंने आशंका जताई कि इज़राइल पर अपने महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा क्षेत्रों और उपलब्धियों से पीछे हटने का दबाव भी डाला जा सकता है.
हालिया युद्ध के दौरान हुए हमलों में आईडीएफ (IDF) का आकलन है कि ईरान की परमाणु क्षमताओं को गंभीर नुकसान पहुंचा है, लेकिन इसके बावजूद तेहरान के पास एक से दो वर्षों में परमाणु हथियार हासिल करने की क्षमता बनी हुई है.
इन सुरक्षा चुनौतियों का हवाला देते हुए प्रधानमंत्री ने केसेट के सदस्यों से अन्य प्राथमिकताओं को छोड़कर एक राष्ट्रीय एकता सरकार बनाने की अपील की और कहा कि केवल ऐसी सरकार ही इन चुनौतियों का मुकाबला करने में सक्षम है.
नेतन्याहू के भाषण के दौरान पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री और बी-याचाद (B'Yachad) के सांसद नफ्ताली बेनेट ने बाधा डालते हुए चिल्लाकर सवाल किया, "आपके कतारी सलाहकारों का क्या हुआ? 7 अक्टूबर की जांच का क्या हुआ?" इस पर वहां मौजूद नेतन्याहू की पत्नी सारा और बेटे यायर ने अस्पष्ट प्रतिक्रिया दी.
दूसरी ओर, यशर (Yashar) पार्टी के अध्यक्ष गदी आइजनकोट ने नेतन्याहू के इस संबोधन की कड़ी आलोचना की.
उन्होंने इस भाषण को "भ्रामक, विभाजनकारी, नफरत से भरा और शर्मनाक" करार देते हुए नेतन्याहू पर शपथ ग्रहण मंच के दुरुपयोग का आरोप लगाया.
आइज़ेनकोट ने कहा कि इस भाषण से यह साफ हो गया है कि प्रधानमंत्री को पद पर एक मिनट भी बने रहने का अधिकार नहीं है. उन्होंने देश की सुरक्षा के लिए खतरा बने नेतन्याहू के शासन को हटाने और एक राष्ट्रीय आपातकालीन सरकार के गठन की मांग की.

Gauteng residents are being urged to take precautions as scorching temperatures grip parts of the province, with emergency services warning of the health risks associated with extreme heat.
The developing El Niño climate pattern is raising concerns about extreme heat and changing rainfall patterns across the region, with parts of Gauteng currently experiencing scorching temperatures.
The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has warned that the 2026/27 El Niño event could bring above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall to much of southern Africa.
In Johannesburg, temperatures will peak at 34 to 36 degrees Celsius in most parts of Johannesburg on Wednesday and Thursday.
Emergency services have urged residents to stay hydrated and avoid direct exposure to sunlight, particularly between 11h00 and 15h00.
Individuals who are working directly in the sunlight are encouraged to take regular break and to seek shade where possible. Prolonged exposure to extreme heat can cause several health complications, including heat cramps and heat exhaustion, which might lead to heat strokes.
Johannesburg Emergency Services spokesperson, Robert Mulaudzi, has called on parents to ensure that children stay away from open bodies of water, dams and rivers to prevent drowning incidents during the hot weather.
The effects of El Niño are expected to extend beyond rising temperatures, with reduced rainfall in southern Africa potentially placing additional pressure on water resources, agriculture and food security.
Meanwhile, countries in East Africa, including Kenya and Somalia, are facing a different climate risk, with forecasts pointing to above-normal rainfall and an increased likelihood of flooding.
The World Meteorological Organisation has warned that the unusually strong El Niño event is disrupting normal weather patterns across the world, increasing the risk of drought in some regions and heavy rainfall and flooding in others.
United Nations Secretary-General, Antonio Guterres, warned that the world has entered a danger zone of extreme weather, as the effects of El Niño intensify.
The climate pattern, which may result in some regions experiencing droughts and others experiencing typhoons, is expected to peak towards the end of this year, although its effects could continue well into 2027.

Emergency services place Gauteng on high alert ahead of mid-week heatwave
Authorities across South Africa’s (SA) Gauteng province are on high alert following severe weather warnings of an impending mid-week heatwave expected to affect Johannesburg and Pretoria this Wednesday and Thursday.
The SA Weather Service announced that temperatures will soar to maximums of 36°C across several regions of the province, prompting City of Johannesburg Emergency Management Services Spokesperson Robert Mulaudzi to issue an urgent advisory warning residents working directly in the sunlight to take regular breaks to prevent heat exhaustion and heatstroke, while pleading with parents to monitor young children near dams and river streams to avoid drowning incidents.
Emergency management officials have also warned of increased pressure on local municipal water infrastructure, urging residents to implement strict water conservation measures and avoid non-essential usage as high consumption levels threaten reservoir capacity during the peak heating period.

articles.title: Why Kenya Is Experiencing Extreme Heat Despite El Niño Forecasts - The Kenya Times
articles.search_term: (heatwave OR "heat wave" OR "severe heatwave" OR "extreme heat" OR "heat spell" OR "scorching heat" OR "blistering heat" OR "sweltering heat" OR "hot winds" OR loo OR "hot loo winds" OR "intense heat" OR "unbearable heat" OR "deadly heat" OR heat OR "weather forecast" OR "weather update" OR "weather alert" OR "IMD forecast" OR "IMD prediction" OR "IMD alert" OR IMD OR "rising temperatures" OR "temperatures expected to rise" OR "relief from heat" OR "respite from heat" OR "heat respite" OR "respite from scorching heat") Chhattisgarh
articles.full_text:
Kenyans across the country continue to experience high temperatures even as the country prepares for the October to December short-rains season, which was forecast to bring above-average rainfall.
The contrasting weather conditions have raised questions about why some areas are experiencing intense heat while others are receiving heavy rainfall, despite forecasts pointing to generally wetter conditions.
Speaking on Spice FM on Wednesday, November 11, Acting Deputy Director of Meteorological Services for the Eastern Region Richard Muita said the situation was linked to different climate systems influencing weather patterns across Kenya and the wider region.
Muita explained that El Niño does not automatically translate into rainfall everywhere, noting that its effects vary depending on geographical conditions and other climate drivers.
“El Niño is just a factor. And therefore, in order for you to attach the interpretation or what it may cause, then you need to tie the science,” Muita said.
Meteorologist Explains Link Between El Niño, Indian Ocean and Kenya’s Extreme Heat
He added that parts of Southern Africa were likely to experience severe drought, showing how the same climate phenomenon can produce different outcomes in different regions.
The meteorologist also pointed to the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), describing it as a major driver of rainfall in Kenya and East Africa.
ADVERTISEMENT
“The Indian Ocean Dipole, for a fact, is the major driver of rainfall in Kenya and East Africa, as opposed to the belief that it is more of El Niño or other factors,” he stated.
Muita explained that the Indian Ocean Dipole played a significant role in the enhanced rainfall experienced between October and December 2018, when several areas, including Nairobi, experienced heavy rains and flooding.
He said rainfall patterns were influenced by a combination of factors, including El Niño, the Indian Ocean Dipole and prevailing ocean temperatures.
Why Some Parts of Kenya Are Hot While Others Receive Heavy Rainfall
Muita said the distribution of rainfall across the country had not been uniform, with some counties recording substantial rainfall while others experienced prolonged dry conditions.
He cited Nyeri and other areas around Mount Kenya, as well as parts of Western Kenya, which had recorded more than 250 millimetres of rainfall by the end of October.
In contrast, residents in Mandera had experienced high temperatures and prolonged dry conditions before flooding was reported in parts of the county.
ADVERTISEMENT
He explained that the contrasting conditions showed why national weather forecasts should not be interpreted as meaning every county would receive the same amount of rainfall at the same time.
Muita maintained that the Kenya Meteorological Department had remained consistent with its August seasonal forecast, which indicated that most parts of the country would receive above-average rainfall during the October to December season.
November is the peak month of the short-rains season, and Muita said the department was continuing to monitor rainfall patterns as the season progressed.
Human Activities Behind Rising Global Temperatures
Beyond the influence of El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole, Muita attributed the sustained increase in global temperatures to climate change and human activities.
He identified the burning of fossil fuels, deforestation and changes in land use, including agricultural activities, as some of the factors contributing to rising temperatures.
Muita explained that human activities release greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, trapping heat and contributing to the warming of the planet.
Using an analogy of covering oneself with additional blankets, Muita explained how greenhouse gases contribute to rising temperatures.
“It’s more like what you do when you cover yourself with more blankets. So we increase the layer that actually obstructs the solar intensity from coming in, and therefore we make the world much warmer than it is supposed to be,” he said.
He also dismissed increased solar intensity as the primary explanation for the warming experienced in recent decades.
“From 1978 up to date, the solar intensity has never increased. It has remained constant,” Muita stated.
He added that major volcanic eruptions could influence global temperatures, but maintained that human activities remain a major contributor to the current warming trend.
Muita said the forecast for above-average rainfall remained under monitoring, emphasising that El Niño should not be confused with rainfall itself.
The Kenya Meteorological Department forecasts El Niño conditions and above-average rainfall across much of the country. A national assessment has identified 18 counties and 5,660 health facilities in at-risk areas, and rates overall flood preparedness at 54 per cent. Key structures are in place, but serious gaps remain.
The department warns that November is usually the peak rainfall month of the short rainy season, which normally lasts from October to December.
A regional forecast from the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) warned in September that there was “an 81% probability of a very strong El Niño during October–December 2026”.
The UN’s migration body the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has also warned that almost 900,000 people could be forced to leave their homes in Kenya this year, mostly because of the predicted floods.
Ahead of the anticipated El Niño-related rainfall, the government established a response committee headed by the Deputy President, while county governments also undertook preparedness measures.
An El Niño Contingency Plan is in place, the Ministry of Health and the National Disaster Operations Centre have activated joint planning meetings, and counties are being supported to assess their own preparedness.
The Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) has been building an emergency medical team for this kind of crisis, a trained group that deploys during disasters to treat the sick and injured and keep essential care running.
Thirty KDF health professionals completed induction training in 2024, and the team now has a leadership structure and written procedures.

Recent rains have offered much needed reprieve from soaring temperatures associated with El Niño, but the City of Ekurhuleni (CoE) still cautions that residents should take necessary precautions to protect themselves against extreme heat.
According to the South African Weather Service (SAWS), the 2026/27 summer season is expected to experience above-normal temperatures and below-avarage rainfall, increasing the risk of heatwaves, water scarcity and veld fires.
“With temperatures expected to rise, the city warns that prolonged exposure to extreme heat can lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially life-threatening heatstroke, particularly among children, older persons and people with underlying medical conditions,” said CoE spokesperson Zweli Dlamini.
Residents are urged to follow these safety precautions:
• Drink water regularly, even when you do not feel thirsty. • Carry drinking water in a bottle when travelling or spending extended periods outdoors. • Avoid excessive alcohol and caffeine consumption, as these may contribute to dehydration. • Eat light meals and include water-rich fruits and vegetables in your diet. • Avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, particularly during the hottest hours of the day. • Wear lightweight, loose-fitting and light-coloured clothing. • Use wide-brimmed hats, sunglasses and sunscreen when outdoors. • Seek shade or remain in well-ventilated, cooler environments whenever possible. • Use a damp cloth, cooling towel or fan to help regulate body temperature.
Residents are further encouraged to seek medical assistance should their experience symptoms associated with heatstroke which include dizziness, headaches, nausea, excessive sweating, weakness and confusion.
While excessive exposure to heat poses significant health risks, it also has a negative effect on water resources.
“Water conservation is everyone’s business as Level 1 water restictions remain in place,” said Dlamini.
“We can all play a part by timeously repairing leaking taps and pipes, avoiding unnecessary water usage and reporting municipal water leaks and burst pipes.”
Residents are further urged to refrain from burning waste or making open fires in dry, windy conditions, as these activities may increase the risk of veld fires.

Pretoria residents should prepare for a scorching stretch of weather, with a heatwave alert forecasting very hot to extremely hot conditions across Gauteng from Wednesday, November 11, to Friday, November 13.
According to the alert, a dominant high-pressure system is expected to drive temperatures above local heatwave thresholds in several regions for three consecutive days.
The affected areas include Gauteng, North West, most of the Free State, parts of the Northern Cape, the Bushveld of Limpopo, the Mpumalanga Highveld and extreme north-western KwaZulu-Natal.
For Pretoria residents, the alert highlights the need to plan outdoor work, school activities and exercise around the expected heat.
The South African Weather Service (SAWS) explains that heatwave thresholds differ between towns and cities. A heatwave may be declared when maximum temperatures reach or exceed 5°C above a location’s average maximum for its hottest month for at least three days.
The supplied alert warns that prolonged exposure to extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially life-threatening heatstroke.
Residents are encouraged to drink water regularly throughout the day, seek shade and spend time in cool, well-ventilated spaces.
Strenuous outdoor activities should be avoided during the hottest hours. The alert also encourages schools to suspend outdoor physical activities during the heatwave.
SAWS advises limiting or avoiding children’s outdoor play between 10:00 and 16:00 during heatwaves. People working outdoors should take regular breaks, wear protective headgear and choose lightweight, loose-fitting clothing.
Parents and caregivers are urged to take extra care of children and older people, while pet owners should ensure their animals have shade and drinking water.
Residents should monitor updated forecasts as the expected hot spell approaches.

In XRP news this week, David Schwartz, one of the designers of the XRP Ledger and Ripple’s chief technology officer emeritus, said on Tuesday that he has sold most of his XRP over the years. He put his peak holding at about 26 million XRP and his current stack at about 3 million.
“It’s not a secret,” Schwartz wrote on X, where he posts as JoelKatz. His Bitcoin and Ethereum went almost to zero too: from about 1,500 BTC to 1, and from about 40,000 ETH to 6.
It's not a secret. I think I'm down from a high of around 26 million XRP to around 3 million XRP. Down from around 1,500 BTC to 1 BTC. Down from around 40,000 ETH to 6 ETH.https://t.co/EnFjk9aXu1
The timing stung. XRP trades at $1.056, down 17% in a week. That is 71% below its July 2025 record of $3.65.
Schwartz says he sold under a simple rule: sell at every new all-time high. We checked how often that rule would have fired. Since its January 2018 peak, XRP has closed at a new record on only two days, both in July 2025.
So did one of XRP’s best-known builders dump on holders?
XRP News: Schwartz Sold Into Rallies, Not Into This Drop
The numbers say he sold slowly, over years. Schwartz gave no dates and no sale prices, so nobody outside knows exactly when the coins changed hands.
He has given the reason before. In a July post, he set out his rule: he “agreed with my wife to sell at every new ATH and I really, really hate risk”.
He added more on Monday, November 9. He said he has “sold nearly all of the digital assets I’ve ever held” and has not bought XRP “in a long time”. He still holds “quite a bit of Ripple stock”, which he called more risk than he would like.
The scale is large on paper:
XRP sold: about 23 million XRP, an 88% cut from his peak.
What is left: about 3 million XRP, worth about $3.2 million at today’s price.
Bitcoin: 1,499 BTC sold. Those coins would be worth about $110 million at today’s price of about $73,800.
XRP trades at $1.056 on Binance, down 2.8% in 24 hours. On Tuesday, after the U.S. inflation report, it fell to $1.0311, its lowest price since August 19.
On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, XRP sits well below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA stands at $1.284 and the 200-day EMA at $1.347.
Resistance: $1.089, the 24-hour high, then $1.130, a recent swing high. Above that, $1.284, the 50-day EMA.
Support: $1.031, Tuesday’s low, then $1.009. Below that, $0.986, the August 14 low and the last time XRP traded under $1.

Three weather stations in Madeira were already recording extreme values corresponding to the orange warning for precipitation until 8 pm, before the weather warnings associated with Storm Charles came into effect, which was expected at 9 pm.

Also on Pico Alto and Monte, rainfall of 23.3 mm/h was recorded, exceeding the threshold of 21 mm per hour that determines that level of warning.
At Pico do Areeiro, rainfall reached 17.4 mm/h and 34.8 mm/6h. At Santa Cruz/Aeroporto, rainfall of 17.4 mm/h was also recorded.

The entire island of Madeira is now under a red warning for precipitation until 6:00 AM on Wednesday.
The Portuguese Institute for the Sea and the Atmosphere (IPMA) has extended the red warning for precipitation to the North Coast of Madeira, due to the forecast of heavy and persistent rain associated with the passage of Storm Charles.
With this update, the entire island of Madeira is now covered by the maximum level of weather warning for precipitation, including the North and South coasts and mountainous regions. The warning came into effect at 9 pm on Tuesday and will remain in effect until 6 am on Wednesday.
The weather situation is expected to worsen during the early hours of the morning, especially in mountainous areas, where a red warning for wind will also be in effect between midnight and 6 am, with gusts that could reach 140 kilometers per hour.
In the remaining areas of the island, the wind will be under an orange warning until midday on Wednesday, with gusts expected up to 100 km/h. In mountainous regions, the orange wind warning predicts gusts up to 130 km/h before and after the red warning period.
From 6 am on Wednesday, the precipitation warning is expected to be lowered to orange across the entire island of Madeira, remaining in effect until 9 am, due to the possibility of heavy rain or showers.
In Porto Santo, IPMA maintains the orange warning for precipitation until 9 am on Wednesday and for wind until noon, with gusts that could reach 100 km/h.
The sea conditions are also expected to worsen, with waves potentially reaching five meters on the south coast of Madeira and 4.5 meters on the north coast and in Porto Santo.

articles.full_text:
Areeiro recorded 47.6 liters per square meter in the last hour and 91.7 liters in six hours.
Until 9 pm, 13 of the 18 weather stations in the network of the Portuguese Institute of the Sea and the Atmosphere (IPMA) on the island of Madeira recorded precipitation values falling within the different levels of weather warnings: yellow, orange and red.
The most significant rainfall was recorded in Chão do Areeiro, with 47.6 mm in one hour and 91.7 mm in six hours, exceeding the red alert thresholds in both criteria.
Particularly significant was the intensity of the rainfall in the last two hours, a period in which 77.3 mm accumulated, a value that, by itself, exceeds the 60 mm threshold defined for a red alert in six hours. In three hours, the accumulated rainfall reached 84.4 mm.
The weather warnings issued by IPMA for the Madeira archipelago came into effect at 9 pm this Tuesday, due to the passage of Storm Charles.
The south coast of Madeira and the mountainous regions are under a red warning for precipitation, due to the forecast of sometimes heavy and persistent rain. This warning extends until 06:00 on Wednesday, then changing to an orange warning until 09:00.
